lean.statement: For measurable spaces A and B, a probability measure μ on A, Markov kernels K and L from A to B, and a real function ε integrable under μ: if for μ-almost every x, every measurable set s satisfies |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x, then every measurable set t satisfies |(K ∘ₘ μ).real t - (L ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤ ∫ x, ε x ∂μ.
approved_definition_context: A Markov kernel maps each input to a probability measure and is measurable in the input for every measurable output event.
Passing a measure through a kernel means integrating the conditional output measures against the input measure.
The real value of an event measure is its extended nonnegative mass converted to a real; for probability measures this conversion is finite and exact.
An almost-everywhere statement may fail on an input-null set, while its following universal event quantifier applies at every remaining input.
